KIREJI POND

MATSUO BASHŌ · 1686

Before the leap, stillness.

古池や
蛙飛び込む
水の音

furu ike ya
kawazu tobikomu
mizu no oto

old pond — ya
a frog jumps in
water's sound

KIREJI POND

THE PRINCIPLE · 切字

The cut.
old pond
ya
a frog jumps in
water's sound

Ya is a kireji, a cutting word. It splits the poem in two: an old, quiet pond on one side, a frog and a sound on the other.

The poem lives in the gap you leap across. English has no cutting words, so we cut with a turn: a dash, a shift, a surprise.
